author: reek
body: A Codex program can create a directory. create-directory was a compiler builtin whose emitter raised CDX2043 and explained that the parent walk and the dot entries were not written. That was honest, and an honest refusal is still a refusal. The name is out of the builtin tables now and the work is in Foreword chapter Fat16, next to write-file and file-exists, for the same reason they are: the machine does not know what a directory is, and FAT16 does.

author: reek
body: This starts from a volume with no subdirectory at all -- unlike fat16-subdir, whose /SUB is built host-side -- so every directory here was made by the code under test. That is the point: the read-back walks a tree this chapter built.

author: reek
body: "twice" must be False. Making a directory that exists would otherwise claim a second cluster and commit a second entry under the same name: two directories, one name, and a walk that finds whichever comes first.

author: reek
body: "nested" and "write-deep" are the ones that would fail if the dot entries were wrong. fat16-poke-dir-entry writes an 8.3 name by splitting on the first dot, which turns "." into an empty base and an empty extension -- eleven spaces. A directory built that way lists fine and cannot be climbed out of, so the dot names are poked as literal bytes instead. Two levels deep is what exercises the walk that would fall over.

author: reek
body: "no-parent" pins the refusal, because writing a directory entry into a parent that does not exist is the corruption this would otherwise cause quietly.
